10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-13b [ED-06, SPK-02 question 3, Platform/SRE (ingress)] — TWO TIMED execution.snapshot EVENTS REACH A REAL BROWSER SEPARATELY, before response closure, through every proxy layer, captured as a HAR from a real browser on the staging hosts. 10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-14 [ED-06, SPK-02 question 4, Platform/SRE (ingress)] — a 15 s HEARTBEAT KEEPS AN IDLE STREAM OPEN across the ingress and any platform proxy, and the EFFECTIVE MAXIMUM STREAM LIFETIME is measured against the intended 60 s. 10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-15 [ED-06, SPK-02 question 5, Platform/SRE (ingress) + backend dev] — RECONNECT WITH Last-Event-ID TO A DIFFERENT API REPLICA restores the current snapshot. The evidence must show the two connections were served by DIFFERENT PODS: a reconnect that happens to land on the same replica proves nothing and is the way this criterion gets reported passed without being tested. Production runs three replicas scaling to six. The design answers this by reading committed state rather than by affinity, and **NO STICKY-SESSION OR SESSION-AFFINITY SETTING MAY BE INTRODUCED TO MAKE IT PASS** — story 10.18b introduced none, and the streaming Ingress it added carries no affinity annotation of any kind. Trading a design property for a deployment workaround would close this criterion by defeating the thing it exists to check.

The DEPLOYMENT half is done: exact-origin credentialed CORS compared against the rendered frontend host in the same manifest, never a wildcard, and no credential in any URL. A DEMONSTRATED GATEWAY INCOMPATIBILITY IS A VALID OUTCOME — it selects the documented GET fallback and changes no execution contract.
